headline: Revenue and profit climb on fleet growth, yields improve
summary_short: Viking's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 16.5% y/y to $2,190.5M and diluted EPS climbed to $1.31 from $0.99, as fleet-driven capacity growth and higher revenue per passenger cruise day lifted Adjusted EBITDA 18.2% to $748.4M even as Occupancy eased 1.2ppt to 94.4%.
summary_long: Total revenue grew 16.5% y/y to $2,190.5M, driven by higher Capacity PCDs from fleet growth (99 vessels vs 90 a year ago) and higher revenue per PCD; Viking Ocean revenue rose faster (+24.2%) than Viking River (+10.6%). Net Yield rose 6.3% to $645 while Occupancy slipped 1.2ppt to 94.4%. Operating expenses rose across all lines on fleet growth, but revenue growth outpaced costs, lifting operating income 18.0% and Adjusted EBITDA 18.2% to $748.4M. Net income rose 33.8% to $587.7M ($1.31 diluted EPS), aided by a currency swing to a $4.7M gain from a $37.2M loss a year earlier. Cash stood at $3,985.4M at quarter-end; the company gave no formal forward guidance beyond disclosed advance-booking metrics.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to higher Capacity PCDs driven by fleet growth (99 vessels vs 90 a year ago) and higher revenue per passenger cruise day.
Filing frames the rise as the net result of revenue growth (16.5%) outpacing the increase in cruise operating and other operating expenses, which rose on fleet growth.
Filing attributes the increase to a $98.4M rise in operating income and a $41.9M favorable swing in currency gain (loss) versus the prior-year quarter.
Not separately explained in the release; tracks the operating-income increase, adjusted for the same currency and share-based-compensation add-backs applied in both periods.
Not explained in the release — no specific cause is given for the 1.2ppt y/y dip beyond general fleet-and-demand management language.
Tracks the net income increase; weighted-average diluted shares were roughly flat (448.1M vs 445.5M y/y), so per-share growth closely mirrors net income growth.

Growth reflects fleet expansion (92 river vessels, 13 ocean ships, 2 expedition ships) lifting capacity across both Viking River and Viking Ocean, plus higher revenue per passenger cruise day, partly offset by softer Occupancy and higher fleet-related costs.

confidence_notes: Filing-depth summary from Viking's Form 6-K (interim H1 2026 financial statements + MD&A) — no separate earnings-call transcript or press release with management quotes was located within this filing, so Step 3c (call snippets) was skipped. KPI values for revenue, operating income, net income, Adjusted EBITDA, Occupancy and Net Yield are read directly off the filing's 'Results of Operations' and 'Selected Operational and Financial Metrics' tables (three-months-ended columns), not the resolver's kpis object, which carried only eps_usd. The resolver's kpis.eps_usd.prior_yy (-$0.24, labeled 'FY2025 Q2') does not reconcile with this filing's own FY2025 Q2 diluted EPS of $0.99: subtracting the filing's three-months-ended FY2025 EPS ($0.99) from its six-months-ended FY2025 EPS ($0.75) implies a Q1 FY2025 EPS of approximately -$0.24, so the shard's stored 'y/y prior' appears to be a mislabeled Q1 figure — flagged here, not corrected in the shard; this summary's EPS y/y KPI uses the filing's own $0.99 comparator instead. The resolver's prior_qq (-$0.12) DOES reconcile: subtracting the filing's three-months-ended FY2026 EPS ($1.31) from its six-months-ended FY2026 EPS ($1.19) implies a Q1 FY2026 EPS of approximately -$0.12, matching the shard exactly and consistent with the company's disclosed seasonality (Q1/Q4 near break-even or loss, Q2/Q3 the profitable months). Adjusted EPS ($1.31) equals GAAP diluted EPS this quarter — no reconciling items. No formal revenue/EPS guidance range appears anywhere in the filing; the company instead discloses Advance Bookings and Capacity-PCDs-sold percentages by season (2026/2027) as forward-looking color, which is narrative rather than a numeric guidance range, so the event's guidance[] array was left untouched.
